headline: Lazio won 3-0 at Juventus, but the margin is the question
summary: Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on Sunday and are unbeaten in Serie A on 19 points. Even so, they created only 0.57 expected goals in Turin, and Parma made 1.61 at home to Torino — the away side is not without chances. Parma have also drawn their last 2 visits to the Olimpico. Across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Lazio are clear favourites: 66.8%, up from 63.0% in recent days. The fair handicap is about a goal in their favour, moved from 1.02 to 1.19, and Over 2.5 goals is 50.8%, almost even.
read: Lazio are unbeaten and second in Serie A after a 3-0 win at Juventus, and the market makes them around two-thirds likely to beat a Parma side sitting 19th and booed off at home by Torino on Sunday. The fair handicap has been pushed to about 1.2 goals in Lazio's favour, with the goal line hovering just above 2.5 — but Lazio's low xG in Turin and two recent draws with Parma at the Olimpico are the notes of caution.

facts.fact: Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on Sunday, the best league start in the club's history according to Gazzetta.
facts.meaning: They arrive at the Olimpico as the form team of the early Serie A season, and they won it away to one of the big names.

facts.fact: Parma are 19th in Serie A with 4 points from seven games, one win, one draw and five defeats.
facts.meaning: They come to Rome in the bottom three and needing a result to stop the slide under a new coach.

facts.fact: Lazio sit second on 19 points from seven games and are still unbeaten in the league.
facts.meaning: This is a side playing with confidence and, unusually for Lazio in recent years, winning the games it should win.

facts.fact: Parma have conceded 10 goals in their last five league games and were booed off at home by Torino on Sunday.
facts.meaning: The away end travels to Rome with a defence that has leaked two goals a game and a team low on confidence.

facts.fact: The market's fair handicap has moved from Lazio -1.02 to -1.19, with the main line now at -1.25.
Lazio created only 0.57 xG in their win at Juventus on Sunday.
facts.meaning: The scoreline flattered them — the chances they made were worth far less than three goals, so the form is better than the performance.

facts.fact: Parma created 1.61 xG at home to Torino — more than Lazio managed in Turin on the same weekend.
facts.meaning: Parma are not toothless: they made chances even in their heaviest defeat of the run.

facts.fact: The market's fair goal total has moved from 2.43 to 2.53, and Over 2.5 is now the slight favourite at 50.8%.
facts.meaning: The market sees a game just above two and a half goals — a genuine coin-flip on Over 2.5 rather than a high-scoring expectation.

sources.fact: Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus in their last Serie A match, with Gattuso's side sitting top of the table alongside Inter after seven matchdays on the best league start in the club's history.
Gattuso warned Lazio not to look at the table yet, saying if they take it one game at a time they can surprise people.
After the Juventus win Gattuso preached caution, telling his players to keep their feet on the ground.
Pundit Massimo Mauro said Juventus played like a Serie D team against Lazio.
Former Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi said Juventus lack a coach and did not turn up in their 3-0 home defeat to Lazio.

Italian outlet Il Tempo reports that Cancellieri has resumed training with the group after an injury picked up on holiday and is heading towards the squad for Saturday's match against Parma, while Gudmundsson is still in pain.
Parma lost 0-3 at home to Torino, their second game under new coach Alberto Gilardino, and were booed off.
SportParma described Parma's defence as horrific in the Torino defeat and said the reaction was confused and late.
